blocks.text: Have you ever encountered a program crash and wondered what went wrong? Understanding errors and exceptions is crucial to writing robust software.

blocks.markdown: In programming, errors are inevitable, but how we handle them can make the difference between a robust application and one that frequently crashes. This lesson will explore the nature of errors and exceptions, and how to effectively manage them in your code.

blocks.title: Error
blocks.text: An error is a problem that occurs during the execution of a program. It can be a syntax error, runtime error, or logical error.

blocks.title: Exception
blocks.text: An exception is a specific type of error that occurs during the execution of a program and can be handled within the code.

blocks.markdown: Errors can be broadly categorized into two types: **recoverable errors** and **programming defects**. Recoverable errors are expected failures that can be anticipated and handled, such as a file not being found. Programming defects, or bugs, are flaws in the code logic that need to be fixed.

rows: Errors in the syntax of the code.
Errors that occur during program execution.
Errors in the logic of the program.
blocks.caption: Types of Errors in Programming

blocks.markdown: Exceptions provide a way to handle errors gracefully. Instead of allowing a program to crash, exceptions can be caught and managed, allowing the program to continue or terminate in a controlled manner.

blocks.latex: try \{ \text{ // code that may throw an exception } \} \ catch (\text{ExceptionType e}) \{ \text{ // code to handle the exception } \}
blocks.caption: Basic Structure of Exception Handling

blocks.title: Handling a Division by Zero Exception
blocks.prompt: Consider a simple program that divides two numbers. How can we handle a division by zero exception?

steps.text: Identify the operation that may cause an exception. In this case, division.
Wrap the operation in a try block.
Catch the specific exception type (e.g., ArithmeticException) and handle it.
steps.latex: catch (ArithmeticException e) \{ System.out.println("Cannot divide by zero."); \}

blocks.answer: By using a try-catch block, the program can handle the division by zero without crashing.

blocks.markdown: Silently swallowing exceptions, where exceptions are caught but not properly handled, can lead to unpredictable program behavior and make debugging difficult. It's important to log exceptions or provide meaningful feedback to the user.

blocks.title: Logging an Exception
blocks.prompt: How can you log an exception to a file instead of just printing it to the console?

steps.text: Open a file writer to the desired log file.
In the catch block, write the exception message to the log file.
Ensure the file writer is closed properly after writing.

blocks.answer: Logging exceptions to a file helps in maintaining a record of errors for later analysis.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.text: Use exceptions to propagate errors to a level that can handle them, and avoid silently swallowing exceptions.

points: Distinguish between recoverable errors and programming defects.
Use try-catch blocks to handle exceptions and prevent program crashes.
Avoid silently swallowing exceptions; instead, log them or provide feedback.
